bib.title: Data Mesh: Topologies and domain granularity
bib.venue: Towards Data Science (saved web page; no date printed)

question: Which data mesh architecture topologies do companies adopt, and what drives each choice?
contributions: Six topologies (scenarios 1-6) differing in domain granularity and in peer-to-peer versus centrally governed distribution, with considerations for each.

results.claim: Fully federated fine-grained mesh is the pure Dehghani form but hard to achieve; needs all domains to conform and duplicates infrastructure.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 1
results.quote:
The fine-grained fully federated mesh is an excellent choice, but hard to
achieve.

results.claim: Topology 1 costs: capability duplication, heavy network use, and cross-domain lookups.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 1
results.quote:
Data gravity and decentralization don’t go hand in
hand.

results.claim: Fully governed mesh puts a central distribution layer in front, fixing data gravity and conformance but slowing time to market and adding coupling.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 2
results.quote:
It will lead to a longer time to market and introduces more
coupling between your domains.

results.claim: Fully governed mesh is chosen mostly by financial institutions and governments.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 2
results.quote:
Most financial institutions and governments implement this
topology

results.claim: Hybrid federated mesh centralises data-product creation, with a platform team sometimes owning products, and consumers more autonomous.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 3
results.quote:
Sometimes, in situations when a domain team
lacks necessary skills or resources, there’s even an enabling or platform
team taking ownership for data products.

results.claim: Value-chain mesh treats a group of closely working domains as one larger domain; central standards apply only across chain boundaries.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 4
results.quote:
Only when crossing the
boundaries of a value chain, there’s adherence to central standards.

results.claim: Coarse-grained aligned mesh domains hold tens or hundreds of applications and tend to duplicate capabilities such as data quality and MDM.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 5
results.quote:
Domains are considered to hold tens or hundreds of
applications.

results.claim: Coarse-grained governed mesh adds a central distribution platform or marketplace and fails without a strong central mandate.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; scenario 6
results.quote:
If the central architecture and
governance team has no strong mandate, these architectures are subject
to fail.

results.claim: No topology is right or wrong; treat data mesh as a framework.
results.setup: Strengholt's observations of customer architecture sessions at Microsoft; opinion, no measurement; conclusion

limits: Anecdotal: based on the author's customer conversations at Microsoft; no counts, sample or measurement.
No publication date in the saved page; figures are not in the text.
Author expects (not shows) multi-cloud difficulty for scenario 2.
Author's employer (Microsoft) and book promotion (Data Management at Scale) are disclosed context.
practices: Make a proper domain decomposition, set application and data ownership, and give strong guidance on data product creation before coarse-grained mesh (Scenario 5).
Capture only unique data, directly from the source of origination, in coarse-grained meshes (Scenario 5).
Use the multiple-workspaces-shared-lake design: domains build in own workspaces, distribute via central storage with domain containers (Scenario 2).
See data mesh as a framework and implement what works best (Conclusion).

terms.definition: you may instantiate many and different small data product architectures for serving and pulling data across domains
Domains manage and create data products in their own workspaces, but the distribution to other domains happens via a central storage layer using domain-specific containers.

lineage.note: Scenario 1 is described as her purest form
lineage.quote:
how Zhamak Dehghani describes data mesh in
its purest theoretical form
